newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SM Summit to issue 10 million new shares.
newsitem.headline: SM Summit to issue 10 million new shares.

text.p: Compact disc maker SM Summit Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it has proposed issuing 10 million new shares to raise money to buy new machinery and pay off some bank loans.
It said in a statement Kay Hian Private Ltd would buy or find buyers for the Singapore $0.10 shares, which would be issued at S$1.04, a 3.7 percent discount over the last traded price of S$1.08.
SM Summit said the new shares represented about 5.33 percent of its issued share capital. The issue was subject to approval of the Stock Exchange of Singapore, the statement said.

It said the company planned to use most of the proceeds to buy machinery for making recordable compact discs and replicating compact discs with just under $3 million destined for the partial settlement of bank loans.
In March, SM Summit reported an 86 percent increase in 1996 net profits to S$10.1 million.
